title.en: Tabulated magnetic-field and flux pressure interpolation
title.zh: 磁场与磁通表格压强插值

summary: Interpolate supplied parallel and perpendicular pressure tables at broadcast magnetic-field and flux queries. A one-dimensional flux table returns one isotropic pressure; a two-dimensional (B, psi) table returns two separately interpolated components.

identity.relation: Caller-supplied pressure tables and magnetic-field/flux query values to interpolated gyrotropic pressure components
identity.direction: (magnetic_field, psi, psi_grid, p_parallel_table, optional p_perpendicular_table, optional b_grid) -> p_parallel, p_perpendicular, is_isotropic, table_dimension
identity.definition: Broadcast finite magnetic_field and psi queries. Without b_grid, require finite nonnegative one-dimensional tables matching a strictly increasing psi_grid; a supplied perpendicular table must equal the parallel table exactly after float64 conversion. Use linear interp1d and return the same pressure components, is_isotropic=True and table_dimension=1. With b_grid, separately bilinearly interpolate finite nonnegative parallel/perpendicular tables on the increasing (B,psi) axes; absent perpendicular data reuse the parallel table. Set is_isotropic to exact equality of the complete supplied component tables and table_dimension=2. Reject negative or nonfinite evaluated pressure. Equal table components describe this prescribed relation, not a thermodynamic proof.
identity.model: Prescribed tabulated isotropic or gyrotropic pressure law with linear one-dimensional or bilinear two-dimensional interpolation; this operator does not derive a pressure law or solve force balance.
identity.geometry: No spatial geometry is reconstructed; magnetic_field and psi query arrays are NumPy-broadcast, with no spatial-axis names or grid topology checked.
identity.coordinates: The first axis of each two-dimensional table is b_grid and the second is psi_grid. The psi axis and queries must use the same caller-supplied flux convention; historical source labels psi in Wb, but this implementation neither checks units nor converts Wb to Wb/rad.
identity.boundary: By default, a query outside either supplied interpolation axis raises. With bounds_error=False, a finite nonnegative fill_value supplies out-of-domain pressure; fill_value=None requests extrapolation, whose result is still checked for finiteness and nonnegativity.
assumptions: Table entries already represent physically appropriate pressures in Pa for the intended plasma and magnetic-field/flux convention.
The caller supplies query values and table axes in matching units and aligned sample order; successful interpolation does not establish equilibrium or thermodynamic consistency.

inputs.name: magnetic_field
inputs.description: Magnetic-field query, used as the first interpolation coordinate only when b_grid is supplied; otherwise used only for broadcasting with psi.
inputs.shape: scalar or array broadcast-compatible with psi
inputs.constraints: All broadcast values must be finite. Positivity and physical field magnitude are not validated.

inputs.name: psi
inputs.description: Flux query at the same broadcast samples as magnetic_field.
inputs.units: same flux unit as psi_grid; historical label Wb
inputs.shape: scalar or array broadcast-compatible with magnetic_field
inputs.constraints: All broadcast values must be finite; coordinate and unit consistency are caller obligations.

inputs.name: psi_grid
inputs.description: Flux interpolation axis shared by both pressure tables.
inputs.units: same caller flux unit as psi
inputs.constraints: Every value must be finite and the axis strictly increasing.

inputs.name: p_parallel_table
inputs.description: Parallel pressure samples on psi_grid or the (b_grid, psi_grid) tensor grid.
inputs.constraints: Must have the branch-specific exact shape and contain only finite nonnegative entries.

inputs.name: p_perpendicular_table
inputs.description: Optional perpendicular pressure samples; the two-dimensional branch reuses the parallel table when absent.
inputs.shape: None or same shape as p_parallel_table
inputs.dtype: real array-like converted to float64 or None
inputs.constraints: Finite nonnegative shape-matched values. Without b_grid, must exactly equal p_parallel_table after float64 conversion; near-equal distinct tables raise instead of being discarded.

inputs.name: b_grid
inputs.description: Optional magnetic-field interpolation axis; its presence selects the two-dimensional branch.
inputs.units: same field unit as magnetic_field, historically T
inputs.dtype: real array-like converted to float64 or None
inputs.constraints: When present, every value must be finite and strictly increasing. Positive field magnitude is not enforced.

inputs.name: bounds_error
inputs.description: Whether any query outside the selected interpolation axis or axes raises.
inputs.constraints: Must be boolean; default rejects out-of-domain queries.

inputs.name: fill_value
inputs.description: Constant out-of-domain pressure when bounds_error=False; None requests extrapolation in that mode.
inputs.dtype: real scalar convertible to float or None
inputs.constraints: When supplied, must be finite and nonnegative. With bounds_error=True, out-of-domain queries still raise.

outputs.name: p_parallel
outputs.description: Interpolated parallel pressure at broadcast queries.
outputs.shape: broadcast shape of magnetic_field and psi, including zero-dimensional scalar result
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative on successful return.

outputs.name: p_perpendicular
outputs.description: Interpolated perpendicular pressure, or a copy of parallel pressure in the one-dimensional branch.
outputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative on successful return.

outputs.name: is_isotropic
outputs.description: Whether the complete supplied component tables are exactly equal after float64 conversion.
outputs.constraints: True for the one-dimensional isotropic path and for equal two-dimensional component tables; unrelated to the interpolation dimension.

preconditions: Finite, strictly increasing interpolation axes and finite nonnegative tabulated pressures with the branch-specific shapes.
Broadcast-compatible finite query values with units and flux conventions matching the table axes.
supported: Linear one-dimensional pressure interpolation in psi with identical returned pressure components.
Bilinear two-dimensional interpolation of supplied parallel and perpendicular pressure on a rectangular (B, psi) table, with bounded fill or extrapolation options.
excluded: Inferring pressure tables from measurements, finding magnetic surfaces or solving magnetic force balance.
Unit conversion between historical Wb and other flux conventions, verifying spatial alignment, or proving an interpolated/extrapolated pressure law physically valid.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for invalid axis rank, length, ordering or finiteness; table shape, finiteness or negativity errors; nonboolean bounds_error; invalid fill_value; nonfinite queries; nonbroadcastable queries; or nonfinite/negative interpolated pressure. NumPy/SciPy conversion and interpolation errors may also propagate.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Out-of-domain queries raise with bounds_error=True. With extrapolation, a nonfinite or negative result is rejected after interpolation; there is no physical fallback or clipping. SciPy/NumPy errors propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root or equilibrium solve is performed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping after an exception. Successful calls return both pressure arrays, exact component-equality metadata and table dimension.

python.signature: evaluate_tabulated_pressure(magnetic_field, psi, psi_grid, p_parallel_table, p_perpendicular_table=None, b_grid=None, bounds_error=True, fill_value=None)

example.description: Interpolate a two-dimensional affine pressure pair and a separate one-dimensional isotropic table.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.closures import evaluate_tabulated_pressure
b_axis = np.array([1.0, 2.0])
psi_axis = np.array([0.0, 1.0])
parallel = np.array([[2.0, 4.0], [4.0, 6.0]])
perpendicular = np.array([[3.0, 5.0], [5.0, 7.0]])
a = evaluate_tabulated_pressure(1.5, 0.25, psi_axis, parallel, perpendicular, b_axis)
np.testing.assert_allclose(a['p_parallel'], 3.5)
np.testing.assert_allclose(a['p_perpendicular'], 4.5)
assert a['is_isotropic'] is False
b = evaluate_tabulated_pressure(10.0, 0.5, psi_axis, [2.0, 6.0])
np.testing.assert_allclose(b['p_parallel'], 4.0)
np.testing.assert_allclose(b['p_perpendicular'], 4.0)
assert b['is_isotropic'] is True
assert a['table_dimension']==2 and b['table_dimension']==1
example.expected: The two-dimensional lookup returns 3.5 and 4.5 Pa, is_isotropic=False and table_dimension=2; the one-dimensional lookup returns 4 Pa in both components with is_isotropic=True and table_dimension=1.

scope: A direct test checks selected two-dimensional bilinear values against supplied pressure tables.
Direct tests check a one-dimensional isotropic limit, the reviewed two-dimensional affine example, and selected invalid fill/extrapolation cases.
Near-equal one-dimensional anisotropy rejection and exact equal-table metadata independent of two-dimensional sampling.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Targeted source regressions, explicit analytic fixtures and a selected no-source installed-wheel replay cover this finite contract. No arbitrary physical-model suitability, continuum convergence, human scientific endorsement or redistribution permission is inferred.
known_limitations: No positive-B or coordinate-alignment check is performed, and the historical psi unit label must not be used to infer a Wb-to-Wb/rad conversion.
Finite nonnegative tabulated values do not ensure nonnegative extrapolation; failing extrapolations raise instead of returning a physical pressure.
Exact component-table equality does not establish thermodynamic consistency or the validity of extrapolation.
